def factor_tail_asymmetry_vol_normalized(df):
    """Downside vs upside tail-return magnitude asymmetry, each tail return scaled by lagged realized vol, preserving parent's economic mechanism while targeting IC/ICIR linearity."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol = ret.rolling(63, min_periods=20).std(ddof=1).shift(1)
    down_tail = (ret < -1.5 * vol) & (vol > 0)
    up_tail = (ret > 1.5 * vol) & (vol > 0)
    down_norm = ((-ret) / vol).where(down_tail, 0.0).rolling(63, min_periods=20).sum()
    up_norm = (ret / vol).where(up_tail, 0.0).rolling(63, min_periods=20).sum()
    raw_asym = -(down_norm - up_norm) / (down_norm + up_norm + 1.0)
    smoothed = raw_asym.ewm(span=5, min_periods=1).mean()
    df_copy["factor_tail_asymmetry_vol_normalized"] = smoothed
    return df_copy["factor_tail_asymmetry_vol_normalized"]
description: Preserves parent's downside/upside tail-return magnitude asymmetry mechanism using lagged 63-day realized vol and ±1.5 sigma thresholds. Mutation changes aggregation from raw tail-return sums to volatility-normalized tail-return sums: each tail exceedance contributes excess return divided by lagged realized vol. This normalization removes volatility-scale effects on raw tail magnitudes, making signal more linear and comparable across stocks, targeting weak IC/ICIR while retaining the downside-jump-heavy ordering and EWM span=5 smoothing that drive RankICIR and payoff stability. Cross-sectional transform remains none.
